message.reasoning_content:
We need answer JSON only. Need evaluate Problem-oriented for each BC story. Need be careful. Need classify violation when story unnecessarily prescribes concrete UI widgets, technical mechanisms, implementation details, algorithms, storage formats, or solution choices instead of stakeholder need. Scope individual. Need one-shot example. Need evaluate all 69. We need produce JSON. Need inspect stories.

We need decide story-by-story. Problem-oriented violation if unnecessarily prescribes solution. Many stories include some UI or mechanism. Need determine.

Let's list all.

BC-001: As anonymoususer, I want to view a list of sponsors, so that I can thank all awesome sponsors.
No solution? "view a list" is need, no concrete UI. No violation.

BC-002: view a list of user profiles. Need. No violation.

BC-003: As trainingcoordinator, I want to email all trainers at once from the website for info and updates, so that It is easier to use. "from the website" maybe solution context? It specifies via website, but stakeholder need is email all trainers. Does "from website" prescription? It is a concrete channel/mechanism maybe, but not necessarily UI widget? Problem-oriented violation when prescribes concrete UI widgets, technical mechanisms, implementation details, etc. "from the website" could be implementation mechanism? But email all trainers at once is need; "from website" may be product context. Is it unnecessary solution? It says from website, not external email. Might be a solution choice (website as mechanism). Need decide. QUS Problem-oriented: specifies problem or need, not solution to it. "email all trainers at once from the website" may include solution (from website) but main need is email. However "from the website" prescribes platform. Could be violation? Let's consider example: using green Save button is concrete UI. "from the website" is not a concrete widget but technical mechanism maybe. Operational says concrete UI widgets, technical mechanisms, implementation details... "from the website" could be technical mechanism/interface choice. But many stories imply website as system. Usually user stories in web project may say "from the website" okay? The criterion wants no solution. "I want to email all the trainers at once from the website" does specify that it happens from website, which is solution context. Might be borderline. We need classify. Could be violation? The need is to email all trainers; "from the website" is a solution choice. But in software requirements, "from the website" can be necessary scope? Hmm.

Need overall pattern: Many stories include UI specifics like "admin view", "checkbox", "link on home page", "WYSIWYG editor", "payment page", "third step", "menu link", "SEO friendly URL path", "page with..." etc. These are definitely solution.

Need evaluate exactly.

Let's go through.

BC-004: "As a attendee, I want to have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are, so that I can make it to class on time." Need is clear map? "map" is a solution representation? A map is a kind of UI artifact. It prescribes a map rather than need "know locations". Is that violation? Yes likely concrete UI solution. Need is to find buildings/rooms; map is solution. Violation? It says "very clear map" is UI mechanism. Yes.

BC-005: "As a trainer, I want to edit my training node myself, so that the training coordinators don't have to and links to slides." This includes "training node" (Drupal implementation detail) and "links to slides" (specific content). Also role: trainer. Need? "edit my training content"? Prescribes technical mechanism "training node". Violation. Evidence "training node", "links to slides".

BC-006: "As a trainee, I want to limit to one registration per day per authenticated user, so that we don't have duplicate spaces." This is a system constraint/rule, not UI mechanism. Need? limit duplicate registrations. Problem-oriented? It specifies a functional rule, not solution implementation. No violation? It's a business rule, not solution? It is solution-ish but need is prevent duplicates. Limit one registration per day per authenticated user is specific policy, but it's stakeholder need? The QUS criterion is problem vs solution. A rule can be requirement not solution mechanism. No violation.

BC-007: "As a trainingcoordinator, I want to have an admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee so that, so that we can see if attendend, refunded, no show." "admin view" is UI solution? It prescribes a view. Need is track registration status. Violation likely. Evidence "admin view". Also duplicate "so that". But criterion not syntax. Yes.

BC-008: "As a attendee, I want to be added to a training waitlist, so that so they can be considered for a class." Need: waitlist. Waitlist is solution? It could be domain solution but not UI implementation. "be added to training waitlist" is stakeholder need maybe. No violation? It doesn't prescribe concrete widget/mechanism beyond domain concept.
